name: Alba Nolasco
life: “I still remember my good cups coming out for everybody except me.” Sunday often includes a stop at the corner by Juniper Tailor, where Alba looks at the things people actually bring in for repair before looking in the display window.
voice: I was too proud to ask for the good cup. I told the new worker which shelf my visitors use.
appearance: Alba is easy to recognize by a neat white crop and one cheek that creases before the other. Usually dressed in a cropped bottle-green coat with a watch on a cracked leather band, Alba touches a knuckle to the chin when searching for a word when listening.
personality: Alba carries anger into a conversation very slowly. Once it arrives, a quiet statement of facts can be considerably harder to sidestep than a shout.
agenda: To get the good cup down at ordinary visits.
family: Alan Chapman is Alba’s first cousin once removed. Alba chooses the music. Alan puts the kettle on. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *Two left slippers*, Alan says, “I sew nonmatching shoes for a dance act. My costume box solved one ordinary morning.”
connections: Geraldine Andrade. A pensioner who wants the good cup and a pensioner who dislikes pet names insist on two different kinds of respect.
